subject: gargoyle
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: cathedral gargoyle crouched on a ledge.
Style: gothic stone carving.

spec.name: Cathedral Gargoyle on a Ledge
spec.description: A snarling gothic stone gargoyle crouched low on a carved cathedral ledge, folded wings rising behind it, ember eyes glowing.
spec.layout: Model space: +Y up, gargoyle faces +Z, ledge slab on the floor. The ledge is a carved stone slab 2.7 x 0.36 x 2.3 m with beveled coping, corbel brackets underneath, and a carved rosette band on its front face. The gargoyle crouches on top of it: heavy haunches at the back (z about -0.4), a hunched ribcage leaning forward, a low snarling head with curled horns and an open jaw at z 0.4-0.8, y up to 1.8; digitigrade arms braced forward on the ledge with clawed knuckles at z about 0.7; digitigrade legs folded under the haunches with clawed feet at z about 0.0; two folded bat-like wings rising up and back from the shoulder blades to y 1.85, spanning x to plus/minus 1.3; a thick tail curling around the right (+X) rear of the ledge with a leaf-shaped spade tip. Gothic carving style everywhere: chiseled facets, deep brow ridges, carved furrow lines on the haunches and chest, small moss patches seated in crevices and on upward stone faces, soot-dark recesses, ember-orange glowing eyes deep in shadowed sockets.

parts.builds: The carved stone ledge the gargoyle crouches on. A main slab built as a loft or frustumBox run from [0,0.14,0] spanning x -1.35..1.35, z -1.15..1.15, in stoneMid. On top of it a beveled coping course of chunky blocks (alternating stoneLight and stoneMid segments) around all four sides, its top surface at y 0.36. Under the front lip, three chunky corbel brackets (tapered frustumBoxes in stoneDark) stepping down to y 0.05. The front face carries a carved band: a row of small rosette bosses (low cylinders in stonePale) separated by dark soot-inlaid grooves (thin soot boxes seated 3 mm proud). Corners of the coping are chipped: small angular missing-corner wedges in stoneDark. Moss grows where stone meets sky: thin irregular moss patches (flat extruded blobs, moss and mossDark) on the top surface near the back edge and seeping over the coping's front rim; a green streak runs down one front corner. The gargoyle's feet and knuckles rest on the coping top at y 0.36, so leave the top clear of tall debris. All stone reads chiseled: box and ngon-section shapes, flat facets, no smooth spheres.
parts.attaches: floor: true; everything else rests on mount ledgeTop (y 0.36).

parts.builds: The gargoyle's core: spine, ribcage, neck, head, face, horns and jaw. Build the torso as a loft over the spine chain (core at [0,0.62,-0.35], chest at [0,0.95,-0.05]): a heavy hunched chest, elliptical sections about 0.55 wide and 0.45 tall at the chest narrowing to 0.3 at the hips, in stoneMid with a countershaded paint - warmLit on up-facing surfaces, stoneDark below and in the hollows. Carved furrow lines: thin soot strips seated along the chest's front and around the shoulders. Two small pebbled pectoral slabs in stoneLight sit on the chest front. The neck is a short thick swept tube from chest to head in stoneMid with a ring of carved fold ridges (thin torus-like swept rings in stoneDark) at its base. The head is a blocky chiseled skull: a stoneLight brow mass with deep overhanging brow ledge (a protruding frustumBox in stoneLight casting the eye sockets into soot), two deep eye sockets holding small glowing ember spheres (ember, glowing via the glow kit, strength 1.6) each with a tiny emberCore glint sphere in front. The muzzle projects forward: a squared snout frustum in stoneLight with flared nostril recesses (small soot wedges), and a wide open mouth built as separate upper and lower jaws: the upper jaw (riding head) carries a row of blocky teeth (teeth, small triangular extrudes) and the lower jaw rides the jaw joint, hinged open about 30 degrees showing a tongue (tongue) and lower teeth, so the mouth can open. Long fangs at the upper jaw corners in teeth. The jaw's underside and throat are stoneDark. Two curled ram-like horns sprout from the head's upper sides: swept tubes (sprout) in clawHorn ridged with thin darker rings, spiraling back and out to about 0.22 m radius. Small carved ear fins behind the horns in stoneDark. The whole head reads as a cathedral spout: the mouth's floor extends forward into a small square spout lip in stoneDark.
parts.attaches: Rises from mount hipSeat over the core and chest joints; shoulders at mounts shoulderL and shoulderR are the limb part's roots; neck and head continue from chest; wings bolt to the back at mounts wingRootL and wingRootR; the tail starts at mount tailRoot.

parts.builds: Arms, legs, hands and feet, all digitigrade and crouched. Arms: from mounts shoulderL and shoulderR (riding shoulderL/R) build thick upper-arm tubes (sweep, stoneMid) forward-down to elbows at [0.42,0.78,0.38] and [-0.42,0.78,0.38], then forearms slightly slimmer (stoneLight tops, stoneMid sides) down to knuckles planted on the ledge at about [0.35,0.40,0.68] and mirrored. Each arm carries carved boulder-like muscle bosses: 2-3 overlapping low spheres or frustum slabs in stoneLight on the upper arm and shoulder, and a soot furrow groove at the elbow crease. Hands are clenched fist-knuckles: a blocky hand mass (frustumBox, stoneLight) with three big forward claw talons per hand (curved swept cones in clawHorn, tips touching the ledge top) plus a small rear dewclaw. Legs: from hipL/hipR build the folded digitigrade crouch - thigh tube forward-up to kneeL/kneeR at [0.37,0.6,0.02] (knee carried high and forward, a big blocky knee cap slab in stoneLight), shin down and back to ankleL/ankleR at [0.35,0.37,-0.22], then the foot segment forward to toeL/toeR at [0.35,0.37,0.05]; feet are broad three-toed claw feet (blocky toe masses in stoneLight) whose talons (clawHorn curved cones) grip over the ledge coping's front edge at y 0.36. Haunches: two large teardrop muscle masses (big flattened spheres or loft blobs in stoneMid with stoneLight tops) flanking the tail root at about x plus/minus 0.33, z -0.45, with carved concentric furrow grooves (thin soot strips) - the classic gargoyle thigh read. Moss flecks (tiny flat moss patches) sit in the ankle creases and on top of the knee caps.
parts.attaches: Arm chains root at mounts shoulderL and shoulderR on the chest; leg chains root at mount hipSeat on the core; every claw tip and foot sole rests exactly on the ledge top (mount ledgeTop, y 0.36).

parts.builds: The folded wings rising behind the shoulders. Each wing roots at mounts wingRootL and wingRootR (riding wingL/wingR): a short muscular upper-arm tube (stoneMid) up and out to wingElbowL/wingElbowR at about [0.62,1.5,-0.5], then a slim forearm folding back down-inward, ending in a small clawed thumb knob (clawHorn spike) at about [0.95,1.1,-0.35]. From the wrist, three bony finger spars fan out folded and back: swept tapering tubes (clawHorn joint knobs, stoneDark membrane surfaces) running down and back toward the haunches, the longest reaching about z -0.85, x plus/minus 1.25. Between the spars, the wing membrane is built with b.membrane between adjacent finger paths (and between the leading-edge arm and the first finger), in soot-dark stone: color stoneDark with countershade paint lifting stoneMid on up-facing panels; membrane thickness about 0.015 with a slight scallop at the trailing edge. Along the leading edge of each wing add two rows of small carved ridge studs (stonePale low cylinders) and a darker trim seam (thin swept soot line). At the membrane roots near the spine, moss patches creep onto the webbing's upper face. Two short back spikes (clawHorn cones) ride the spine between the wing roots, and a small ornamental carved finial disc (stonePale lathe rosette) caps each elbow joint. Wings read as carved stone sheets: angular, thick-edged, faceted.
parts.attaches: Wing roots bolt to the torso's back at mounts wingRootL and wingRootR, riding joints wingL, wingElbowL, wingR, wingElbowR; the folded membranes fall behind the arms and over the haunches without touching the ledge top.

parts.builds: The tail curling around the right (+X) rear corner of the ledge. Build a chain over tail1..tail3..tailTip and sweep it: thick at the root (radius about 0.09 at tail1) tapering to 0.03, sections as 6- or 8-sided ngon for the chiseled stone look, color stoneMid with countershade (warmLit on top, stoneDark beneath). Ridges: thin swept soot rings at each joint, and a dorsal row of small triangular carved spikes (stoneDark frustum spikes) along the top of the first two thirds. The last third is plain, ending in a leaf-shaped stone spade tip: a flat extruded diamond blade in stoneLight (about 0.16 long, 0.1 wide, thickness 0.02) with a carved center groove (thin soot strip seated in it), angled upward at about 30 degrees like a scorpion's barb. The tail path: from tailRoot [0,0.55,-0.62] back and down to [0.33,0.45,-0.9], out along the ledge's back-right to [0.58,0.44,-0.75] then curling forward to tailTip [0.75,0.5,-0.15], the whole tail resting on the ledge top (its lowest points at y 0.36, sinking no more than 2 cm into the coping). Moss flecks on the tail's upper surface near the root and one moss tuft where the tail meets the haunch.
parts.attaches: Roots at mount tailRoot on the core joint; rides joints tail1, tail2, tail3, tailTip; the tail's underside lies on the ledge top at y 0.36 within the ledge's back-right quadrant.

calls.reasoning:
I need to write a spec for a cathedral gargoyle crouched on a ledge, gothic stone carving style. Split into 3-6 parts: e.g. ledge/plinth, body (torso+head), wings, arms+claws, legs+haunches, tail.

Coordinate plan: gargoyle crouches on ledge, facing +Z. Ledge is a stone slab on the floor (floor: true). Gargoyle crouched: haunches down, knees up, arms forward braced on ledge, wings folded up behind, horns, snarling face, tail curling around.

Size: maybe 2.6 wide (wingspan), 1.8 tall, 2.2 deep. Ledge maybe 1.9 x 0.25 x 1.6, sitting on floor. Gargoyle on top of ledge, so gargoyle floor: false; ledge floor: true.

Layout numbers:
- Ledge: box from [-1.3, 0, -1.1] to [1.3, 0.35, 1.1]. Stone slab with carved corbels/gargoyles faces trim.
- Body: haunches at rear (z negative? front faces +Z so crouched leaning forward, haunches at back z ≈ -0.5, chest forward z ≈ 0.4). Body region z from -0.7 to 0.7, y 0.35 to 1.5.
- Head: y 1.0-1.7, z 0.3-0.8 with horns.
- Wings: folded, from back y 0.8-1.7, x -1.3..1.3, z -0.7..0.1.
- Arms: from shoulders forward down to ledge, claws at z ~0.9, y ~0.4 (on ledge top).
- Legs: haunches, digitigrade, feet on ledge top at z ~ -0.6, y 0.35.
- Tail: curling to the side along ledge top.

Joints: root joint "haunches" (spine), spine, chest, neck, head, jaw; wings joints (hinge? wings role), arm chains, leg chains, tail. Keep it moderate. The spec lists joints with role from system prompt list: spine neck head jaw hinge tail leg arm wing digit tentacle fan.

Joints list: parents first, one root.

- root: "core" at [0, 0.8, -0.15], dir [0,1,0], role spine? Actually root could be "haunch" role spine.
- spine1, chest, neck, head, jaw.
- armL chain: shoulderL, elbowL, wristL; digits claws.
- legL: hipL, kneeL, ankleL, toeL.
- wingL: shoulder... role wing; wing fingers digit.
- tail: tail1..tail3 role tail.

Keep joints list maybe ~20. Each part lists which joints it rides.

Parts (4-5):
1. ledge — the stone ledge/plinth: floor true, box [-1.35, 0, -1.15] to [1.35, 0.36, 1.15]. Budget 140. Includes carved coping, corbel brackets, drip moulding, moss, chip details.
2. torso — body chain + ribcage + chest + head + face + horns + jaw. Joints: core, chest, neck, head, jaw. Box [-0.55, 0.35, -0.75] to [0.55, 1.75, 0.85]. Budget 200.
3. limbs — arms + legs + claws, digitigrade crouch. Joints arm/leg chains. Box covering shoulders to feet. Budget 180.
4. wings — folded membrane wings with fingers. Box [-1.3, 0.6, -0.85] to [1.3, 1.8, 0.25]. Budget 160.
5. tail — curling tail with spade tip + back ridge spines. Budget 80. Could merge tail into torso or wings. Maybe 5 parts, budget sums to 900 max. 140+200+180+160+80 = 760, fine — could raise. Let's make budgets: ledge 160, torso 220, limbs 200, wings 180, tail 100 = 860.

Mounts: ledgeTop [0, 0.36, 0], shoulder? Actually mounts are where parts meet:
- ledgeTop: [0, 0.36, 0] — limbs and torso rest on it.
- haunchSeat: [0, 0.5, -0.45]? The torso meets limbs at hips [0, 0.72, -0.3].
- shoulderMountL/R? Wings attach at back: wingRoot [0, 1.25, -0.35].
- Maybe keep mounts: ledgeTop, hipSeat, wingRootL, wingRootR, tailRoot.

Palette (max 24): stone greys: stoneDark "#4a4d57", stoneMid "#6b6e78", stoneLight "#8d9099", stonePale "#a8abb2", moss "#4d6b3a", mossDark "#35512a", ink "#1c1d24", eyeEmber "#ff8c2e" (glowing eyes — gothic), tongue "#7a3b4a", clawHorn "#c9c2ae", gold? maybe not. Add warmer lit stone "#9a9284"? Keep ~12 colors.

Style: gothic stone carving — weathered stone, chisel facets, carved linework, moss in crevices, glowing ember eyes (lamps), gargoyles are waterspouts — could include a spout mouth. Stylized blocky.

Builder names: ledge, torso, limbs, wings, tail.

Write layout description carefully: front to back: face at +Z, arms braced forward, chest raised, haunches at back, wings folded rising behind, tail curling around the right side of the ledge.

Joints with positions:
- core (root): at [0, 0.62, -0.35], dir [0,1,0], role spine. Actually root joint should be spine root at haunch. dir along spine forward-up.
- chest: parent core, at [0, 0.95, -0.05], dir [0, 0.55, 0.85] (leaning forward), role spine.
- neck: parent chest, at [0, 1.15, 0.25], dir [0, 0.6, 0.8], role neck.
- head: parent neck, at [0, 1.32, 0.42], dir [0, 0.35, 0.94], role head.
- jaw: parent head, at [0, 1.28, 0.52], dir [0, -0.2, 0.98], role jaw.

Arms: shoulderL at [0.34, 1.12, 0.05]... Actually creature's left is +X. shoulderL [+0.34, 1.08, 0.0], dir down-forward [0, -0.6, 0.8]; elbowL [0.42, 0.78, 0.35]; wristL [0.34, 0.45, 0.7] role arm; digit joints for claws — maybe skip explicit digit joints, note claws as geometry on wrist. But spec asks joints to be listed; keep wrist as chain tip. Claws ride wrist.

Legs: hipL [0.3, 0.7, -0.35] dir down; kneeL [0.4, 0.5, -0.15] (knee forward/up since crouched digitigrade, knee points forward-up); ankleL [0.36, 0.36, -0.5]; toeL [0.36, 0.36, -0.2]? Hmm, crouched: thigh up forward, knee high, shin down back, foot forward. Keep simple: hip [0.3, 0.68, -0.35], knee [0.36, 0.62, 0.05] (knee raised forward), ankle [0.34, 0.38, -0.25] (shin back down), toe [0.34, 0.37, 0.05]. role leg.

Wings: wingL shoulder at [0.22, 1.18, -0.3] role wing; maybe two joints per wing: wingL root and wingL mid, folded upward. dir [1, 0.5, -0.4] then [1, 0.9, -0.2].

Tail: tail1 [0, 0.55, -0.6], tail2 [0.3, 0.42, -0.85], tail3 [0.55, 0.4, -0.55], tailTip [0.6, 0.42, -0.2] role tail, curling around the left side.

Roles from allowed list: spine neck head jaw hinge tail leg arm wing digit tentacle fan. Good.

Parts' joints lists: torso: core, chest, neck, head, jaw. limbs: armL, elbowL, wristL, armR... names must be specified in joints list. Let me finalize names:

- core (root, spine) [0,0.62,-0.35]
- chest (parent core, spine) [0,0.95,-0.05]
- neck (parent chest, neck) [0,1.15,0.25]
- head (parent neck, head) [0,1.32,0.42]
- jaw (parent head, jaw) [0,1.26,0.5]
- shoulderL (parent chest, arm) [0.33,1.08,0.02] dir [0,-0.55,0.83]
- elbowL (parent shoulderL, arm) [0.42,0.78,0.38]
- wristL (parent elbowL, arm) [0.35,0.44,0.68]
- same R mirrored (x negative)
- hipL (parent core, leg) [0.3,0.66,-0.32] dir [0.1,0.35,0.9]? dir should be bone direction from hip to knee: knee raised forward: dir [0, 0.25, 0.97].
- kneeL (parent hipL, leg) [0.37,0.6,0.02]
- ankleL (parent kneeL, leg) [0.35,0.37,-0.22]
- toeL (parent ankleL, leg) [0.35,0.37,0.05]
- mirrored R
- wingL (parent chest, wing) [0.24,1.2,-0.3] dir [0.85,0.55,-0.25]
- wingLMid? maybe wingELbow... call wingElbowL [0.62,1.5,-0.5] dir [0.75,0.65,-0.15]. Also wing tip finger joints? Keep 2 joints per wing plus note membranes. Actually folded wing: arm goes up and out, then forearm folds down. wingL root dir up-out-back; wingElbowL dir down-back. Fine.
- tail1 (parent core, tail) [0,0.55,-0.62] dir [0.35,-0.15,-0.92]
- tail2 [0.33,0.45,-0.9] dir [0.9,0.05,-0.2]
- tail3 [0.58,0.44,-0.75] dir [0.55,0.1,0.83]
- tailTip [0.75,0.5,-0.15] dir [0.3,0.3,0.9]

That's 4+8+4+4 = 20 joints. Good.

Boxes:
- ledge: [-1.35, 0, -1.15] to [1.35, 0.36, 1.15], floor true.
- torso: [-0.55, 0.36, -0.7] to [0.55, 1.8, 0.85].
- limbs: [-0.75, 0.36, -0.65] to [0.75, 1.2, 0.95]. Arms extend to z 0.95, feet. Overlaps torso sides — boxes should meet/share faces but arms attach at shoulders. It's fine for boxes to overlap a bit? Spec says parts that meet share box faces; roughly keep them adjacent. Limbs box [-0.62, 0.36, -0.65] to [0.62, 1.15, 1.0].
- wings: [-1.35, 0.7, -0.9] to [1.35, 1.85, 0.1].
- tail: [0.0, 0.36, -1.15] to [0.95, 0.62, -0.1].

Mounts:
- ledgeTop: [0, 0.36, 0]
- hipSeat: [0, 0.66, -0.35]
- shoulderLine? For limbs-torso connection: shoulderMount: [0.33, 1.08, 0.02] both sides — single mount point can't be two... use mounts shoulderL [0.33,1.08,0.02], shoulderR [-0.33,1.08,0.02]. And wingRootL [0.24,1.2,-0.3], wingRootR mirrored. tailRoot [0,0.55,-0.62].

That's mounts: ledgeTop, hipSeat, shoulderL, shoulderR, wingRootL, wingRootR, tailRoot. Fine.

Part descriptions must be detailed so independent builders match. Include construction guidance: chains/sweeps, blocky chiseled look, colors per piece, details (moss, carved rosette, rivets of stone).

Write the JSON.

I'm planning the wing structure using flat colors and simple geometry, setting up joints for the wing base, elbow, and wrist, then building finger chains to form the wing frame.

Now I'm working out the coordinates for each wing side: shoulder, elbow, and wrist positions, then figuring out where the finger tips land relative to the body. I'm mapping out which membrane panels connect the arm and fingers—leading edges, trailing edges, and body connections—to form the webbing between them.

Setting up finger chains with named joints for the wing skeleton, using membrane connections between adjacent fingers and the body polyline. For the arm, I'm sweeping capsule shapes between shoulder and elbow joints for the upper arm, then continuing into the forearm.

Computing the extrude orientation for moss patches so thickness runs vertically, placing them just above the membrane near the wing root where it's roughly flat.

Thinking about how to get the actual membrane surface for raycasting, since I'm not sure exactly what shape membrane returns -- I'll try surfacing off the root and ray-casting downward, accepting that it might occasionally hit the wrong part, with a fallback to skip if nothing's found.

For placement, I'll use a flat six-sided cylinder stuck onto the hit point for the moss. I'm adding back spikes as cones along the spine near the chest bone, and a finial disc at the elbow made with a lathe profile that builds a small flared disc shape pointing outward. Colors will pull from the stone palette.

Membrane panels get a mix of dark and mid stone tones for variety, with soot for the inner surfaces, skipping extra ridge ribs for simplicity. For the wing fingers, each joint chain gets a unique name per side and side index, using two bone names plus a three-point polyline to form the tip. Skipping any ember glow effect, moving on to writing the code now.

I'm planning out the buildLimbs function, working through the joint positions for each side of the body like shoulders and figuring out the symmetric coordinates needed.

I'm figuring out the geometry per limb segment, using capsules for arms and legs attached to their respective bones, and sketching out a hand box positioned at the wrist with proportions that fit the forearm.

I'm adding curved claw sweeps from the hand front that taper to pointed tips touching the ledge, plus a small rear dewclaw. For the leg, I'm defining capsule segments for thigh and shin with tapering radii, and planning the foot as a box anchored to the ankle so its sole rests on the ledge.

Still shaping toes and claws...

Now I'm positioning the haunches as a flattened sphere near the hip, scaling it to get the right proportions.

I'm layering furrow details onto the haunch surface, computing points along concentric arcs projected onto the ellipsoid to give it a carved, textured look.

Now I'm checking the haunch box bounds so nothing extends past the body silhouette, then adding muscle bosses -- shoulder, upper-arm, and a small elbow furrow ring -- as subtle sphere accents for anatomical definition.

For the elbow I'll use a thin torus oriented along the bone direction instead of a swept ring, then add a rotated box for the knee cap plus tiny flecks of moss near the knee and ankle creases for texture variation, and consider a thin stoneLight highlight capsule on top of the forearm.

Now I'm writing helper functions: a mirror function that flips the x-coordinate for symmetry, a part/bone naming convention, a capsule function with color and bone options, and a claw helper that curves from base to tip using a raised control point for a bezier-like bend.

Still shaping the hand and foot pieces...

I'm planning out the torso-building function using flat colors and the available builder methods like loft, sweep, and frustumBox, while figuring out how to handle the Ctx type signature.

For geometry, I'm sketching out joint positions for hips, core, chest, neck, head, and jaw, then working out loft stations with their positions, widths, and heights to shape the torso from hips up through the chest. I'm considering how to add countershading through separate warm-lit dorsal and belly pieces rather than paint, since I'm unsure whether loft supports sectioned coloring directly.

I'm leaning toward using a sweep with a radius function and sector-based coloring instead of loft, bonding it to the core-chest joint chain, then figuring out how to place rib furrows as thin rods or surface-hugging sweeps across the chest using ray-casting from a front-facing point to find surface contact locations.

Writing surface hit helper...

I'll derive the frame from the path's tangent at each point for ridge placement along the neck, then shift to the head: positioning the skull as a tapered frustum box with a slightly inset top, using stoneMid for the skull and stoneLight for the brow.

Now I'm working out the brow ledge, eye sockets, and glowing embers beneath them — placing soot-colored boxes for the sockets with small ember spheres and glint highlights nested deeper under the overhanging brow, then moving on to shape the muzzle as another tapered frustum.

Continuing into the lower jaw and snout, I'm placing nostril boxes near the front and sketching the upper teeth as a row of small triangular extrusions along the underside of the muzzle, spaced symmetrically from the centerline.

I'm then setting up the jaw joint position and figuring out the hinge rotation to open the mouth, trying to reason through whether parts built after a joint pose inherit the new rotated coordinate space or stay in original model space.

Tongue length and lower teeth placement... the teeth need to sit just above the lower jaw top, and I'm checking that rotating 30° about the jaw pivot creates a believable gap opening between upper and lower teeth without them clipping when closed. I'll add a jaw hinge bone with a rear connecting portion so the rotation reads naturally.

Now adjusting the skull box so it doesn't overlap the jaw bone underneath — lowering the skull center and recalculating its bottom edge, then checking that the brow and eye sockets still fall within reasonable bounds relative to the skull's top and back extents.

I'm also repositioning the muzzle and lower jaw so the teeth don't visibly collide with the muzzle when closed, adjusting jaw center/top height and teeth extent, then setting the spout lip position. After that I'm moving on to sprouting the torso horn with a spiral path configuration.

Still shaping the horn geometry...

Now I'm sketching small ear fins behind the horns as flat triangular extrusions, positioned near the top of the head and colored stoneDark, attached to the head bone.

Next I'm working on cheek ridges and a nose bridge rod along the snout, plus angled brow pieces using rod frustums for the brow mass, then planning moss patches as flattened blob extrusions on the skull and shoulders.

Defining more body geometry...

Still writing geometry helpers...
